system_description: Player choices allow Max Caulfield to express romantic interest in Chloe Price and pursue a same-gender relationship path.
limitations: The affordance is tied specifically to Max and Chloe rather than a general dating system, and the relationship can remain narratively ambiguous depending on player choices.
notes: Parallel system record for the player-enabled relationship path; Max and Chloe remain separate character records.

game_title: Life is Strange: Before the Storm
system_description: Player choices allow Chloe Price to express romantic interest in Rachel Amber and pursue a same-gender relationship path.
limitations: The affordance is limited to the Chloe and Rachel storyline and does not provide a general romance-selection system.
notes: Parallel system record for the player-enabled relationship path; Chloe and Rachel remain separate character records.

system_description: Player choices allow Sean Diaz to pursue a romance with Finn McNamara, pursue a romance with Cassidy, or pursue neither relationship.
limitations: The available routes have unequal amounts of content, and the game does not present sexuality as a labeled character-creation setting.
notes: Recorded as gender-independent romance rather than sexuality customization because orientation emerges through narrative choices.

system_description: Player actions can encourage and unlock the romantic relationship between the NPCs Alphys and Undyne.
limitations: This is a single scripted relationship branch involving NPCs, not a reusable dating or character-romance system.
notes: Kept separate from the Alphys and Undyne character records so the player-enabled affordance is not counted as an additional character identity.

system_description: Player-directed Sims can form romantic and sexual relationships with other Sims without a same-gender prohibition.
limitations: Relationships still depend on successful social interactions and sufficient relationship scores; this record describes the original base game rather than later marriage or customization features.
notes: The archive reports same-gender romance options across every main installment in the series.

system_description: Player-directed Sims can pursue romantic and sexual interactions with Sims of the same or another gender.
limitations: Romantic success is affected by relationship scores, gender preference, chemistry, turn-ons, and turn-offs.
notes: Recorded separately from the game's gender-preference and joined-union systems.

system_description: Player-directed Sims can pursue romantic and sexual interactions with Sims of the same or another gender.
limitations: Romantic success depends on relationship progression and the Sims' evolving preferences.
notes: Recorded separately from sexuality preference, marriage, and expansion-based reproduction systems.

system_description: Player-directed Sims can pursue romantic and sexual interactions with Sims of the same or another gender.
limitations: Later updates added explicit sexual-orientation settings; this row records the broader gender-independent romance affordance rather than those settings.
notes: Recorded separately from gender customization, reproductive-role customization, and marriage.
discovery_source: LGBTQ Video Game Archive; Electronic Arts

system_description: A Sim's gender preference operates on a sliding scale that affects autonomous behavior and responses to romantic or sexual advances, and it can shift through gameplay interactions.
limitations: Preference is shaped through interaction rather than selected through a contemporary labeled sexual-orientation menu.
notes: The source describes gender preference as part of character design and as a dynamic value influenced largely by player-directed actions.

system_description: A Sim's gender preference affects romantic autonomy and responses and can be changed through romantic interactions during play.
limitations: Preference is inferred and shaped through gameplay rather than chosen through a contemporary labeled sexual-orientation menu.
notes: The gender-preference system documented for The Sims 2 continued into The Sims 3.

system_description: Same-gender couples can formalize their relationship through a joined union that is procedurally similar to marriage.
limitations: The game labels the option joined union rather than marriage and awards fewer aspiration points than heterosexual marriage.
notes: The unequal terminology and aspiration reward are retained as limitations rather than presenting the system as equivalent representation.

system_description: Any eligible couple can marry after reaching the required romance and friendship levels, including same-gender couples.
limitations: Marriage remains conditional on relationship progression and the couple not already being engaged or married.
notes: The game uses the marriage label for couples regardless of gender.

system_description: Any eligible couple can marry after reaching the required romance and friendship levels, including same-gender couples.
limitations: Marriage remains conditional on relationship progression and the couple not already being engaged or married.
notes: The game uses the marriage label for couples regardless of gender.

system_description: A couple can engineer a baby at the hospital by splicing both Sims' genes regardless of their genders, producing a child genetically related to both parents.
limitations: The affordance requires the Into the Future expansion and future-world reproductive technology; it does not use WooHoo or pregnancy.
notes: Recorded as queer family creation rather than a general pregnancy system.

system_description: Create a Sim allows physical frame, clothing preference, voice, hairstyle filters, reproductive role, and toilet behavior to be configured with fewer restrictions from the Sim's selected gender.
limitations: The 2016 implementation retained a binary top-level gender selection and did not provide the full customization menu for children; later updates expanded other identity settings.
notes: Available through the June 2016 base-game update and subsequent versions.
discovery_source: LGBTQ Video Game Archive; Electronic Arts
platform_version: Base game update June 2016 or later

system_description: Create a Sim separates reproductive role from the selected gender, allowing a Sim to become pregnant, make other Sims pregnant, or do neither.
limitations: The affordance depends on player configuration and does not by itself define the Sim's gender identity or sexual orientation.
notes: Recorded separately from broader gender-presentation customization because it directly changes family-creation possibilities.
discovery_source: LGBTQ Video Game Archive; Electronic Arts
platform_version: Base game update June 2016 or later

system_description: Character creation allows the player to select a woman or man Avatar.
limitations: The selection is binary and does not document pronoun, body, presentation, or non-binary customization; it should not be interpreted as comprehensive queer character creation.
notes: Ultima VI is documented as the first main-series installment to offer the Avatar gender selection.

system_description: The player can pay Andreas or Wanda for a sexual encounter regardless of the Avatar's selected gender.
limitations: This is transactional sex rather than romance, and willingness to provide a service is not treated as confirmation of either NPC's sexual orientation. The historical source title uses terminology that Press Q does not adopt as a category.
notes: Recorded as a gender-independent sexual-encounter affordance and kept separate from the two ambiguous character records.

system_description: At the Baths in Buccaneer's Den, the player can select the services of male or female sex workers regardless of the Avatar's gender.
limitations: This is a paid sexual encounter rather than a romance system and does not establish the workers' identities or orientations.
notes: No character rows were created because the cited bath-house workers are not individually identified.

game_title: Ultima VII Part Two: Serpent Isle
system_description: Frigidazzi initiates a sexual encounter with the Avatar regardless of the Avatar's selected gender.
limitations: The scene contains coercive behavior when the player rejects her advance and may reflect a male-default script that was not changed for a woman Avatar; it is not classified as a romance system.
notes: Parallel system record for the gender-independent encounter; Frigidazzi remains a separate ambiguous character record.

system_description: The Go All The Way quest allows the player-character to have a sexual encounter with Sven regardless of the player-character's gender.
limitations: This content belongs to the nonprofit fan remake Ultima V: Lazarus and is not present in the original 1988 Ultima V.
notes: Recorded as a gender-independent sexual encounter rather than a labeled romance or sexuality system.
discovery_source: LGBTQ Video Game Archive; Team Lazarus

system_description: Players using either Kassandra or Alexios can pursue available romanceable NPCs regardless of the player-character's selected gender; the romance scenes follow the same structure apart from the player character.
limitations: The options are unevenly distributed and have been criticized for stereotypes and for treating queer and non-queer routes as interchangeable. The original Shadow Heritage episode of the Legacy of the First Blade DLC forced the protagonist into a heterosexual relationship and parenthood regardless of prior choices; a later patch allowed the relationship to be framed as non-romantic but retained the required bloodline outcome.
notes: Kassandra and Alexios are not coded here with fixed sexualities because the represented outcomes depend on player choice. This row records the game-level affordance and its documented contradiction instead.
platform_version: Base game; patched Legacy of the First Blade DLC
